# Our Lady of Sorrows

44 reviews

## Info

Parish-run Father Felix Varela Food Pantry, named after the 19th-century Apostle of Immigrants in New York, provides free groceries to community members. This is part of a broader parish effort that includes a book pantry and a soup kitchen, and is supported by partners like St. John's Bread & Life and Catholic Charities Brooklyn and Queens. It serves anyone in need.

 ## Requirements

  + First come, first serve: open until food runs out
 ## Offerings

  + Free Groceries
  + Other social services available

## Schedule

 Today

  Soup kitchen (ready-to-eat meals): 6:00 pm–7:30 pm
 Fri, October 16th (next week) [...] What do I have to bring?

Every location is different! Please review the details included on each resource to see whether you need to bring any documentation like ID or proof of address, or supplies like bags to carry the food. If you don’t see any information on the resource, you don’t have to bring anything!

Do I need an appointment?

No appointment needed! Just show up to Our Lady of Sorrows during operating hours — no pre-registration required.

What kind of food do they have?

Food pantries like Our Lady of Sorrows offer grocery-style items such as canned food, fresh produce, and dry goods like pasta or rice that you can cook yourself. All of these locations may have different options on different days, so it is hard to tell what each one of them will offer any given day.

# Services Provided

 Weekly Grocery Deliveries for low-income families

  + Pre-registration is required
  + Households must live in the Elmhurst or Corona neighborhoods
  + Currently we are not adding new deliveries to our route however occasionally there are openings as families move off the list. Individuals interested in being contacted in the future can fill out the interest form HERE.
 Walk-in Pantry Bags

  + Walk-ins welcome during program operation hours
  + ID not required
 Hot Meals-To-Go for the Homeless

  + Walk-ins are welcome during program operation hours

IMG_9022.jpg

bottom of page [...] Our Food Pantry serves the Elmhurst and Corona community’s homeless and low-income residents with hot meals-to-go and weekly deliveries of non-perishable food and fresh produce to those that continue to be food insecure. Nearly two in three children in Elmhurst and Corona live in households in or near poverty and wage earners typically work disproportionately in lower-wage professions mainly in construction and hospitality-related sectors. 62% of Elmhurst and Corona residents are rent burdened, a higher rate than residents citywide. Rent burdened households pay more than 30% of their income for housing and may have difficulty affording food, clothing, transportation and health care. Since the pandemic, many are still unemployed or are working reduced hours. [...] top of page
